what_it_does: Health reaches 0 below the armour, barrier and mitigation stack; if nothing refuses it the hero falls through `_die()`. The recap books the delta below the refusals, so a refused death is never a killing blow.
A damage-over-time tick is the same door with fewer refusals on it: four lethal refusals sit on the strike alone (`docs/state.md`, FOUND AT FW), then `_die()`.

Hold the Line's `undying` status leaves him at 1; Undying Rage, a dormant field, once a battle; `_ashes_guard` (Ashes of Al'ar) and `_holy_reversal` (Intercession and Martyrdom) hand health back. Rite of Return and Bear the Brunt answer the same blow through their callbacks. A refused death is no fall.

`dead` set, with no guard against a body already dead, so a second death books a second fall; Broken cleared; a borrowed Constitution returned; a Burn snapshotted for what reads it; the death callback; every composition ended and logged; every status and display chip cleared; the plate greyed; the death animation played. `_die()` and `revive()` are the only two writers of `dead`.

Books the fall for the readout; re-reads every condition on who stands (`_reread_live`), so Empty Pulpit, Dead Air and Dirge switch on at the fall, with a log line; the Oathkeeper's bond passes on from a bound hero, or ends with the Cleric, who binds again if he is raised.
`alive` filters him out, so he takes no turn; his clock and his cooldowns stand as they were until he is raised.

door: who can be struck or picked
what_it_does: He leaves the side enemies target and allies help, so no enemy aims at him and no ally card offers him (`_ally_pick_pool` reads this list). A taunt on a fallen Warrior binds nobody.

A Burn or Poison he laid on an enemy goes on burning: it stands on the enemy, not on him (the glossary's *fallen* entry). Burning Ground stops, because it burns at the start of his own turn, while the ground he laid goes on healing the others.

A companion strikes alongside its hunter's blow, so a fallen Hunter's companion stands and can be struck and strikes no more. `_check_end` counts `heroes` alone: a companion standing does not hold a fight open.

Raises a fallen hero at 50% of maximum health, costs no turn, sets his clock one basic swing past the current hero's, leaves his resource as it stood. The button is lit only while a hero is down. The bot never uses it.
Raises one fallen hero at 25% health and resource, or whole with Renewal when Empowered. Drafted, offered only with Mercy slotted (its `ENGINE_READ` row).
`dead` cleared, health set, the meter emptied, the plate restored; the revive callback re-reads every condition on who stands (`_on_unit_revived`), so a crest switches back the moment he rises.
Writes `member.hp = 0` to the save as the fall lands, so a quit cannot take it back. Not in a sim, and not once the fight is decided.
A fight is won when every enemy is down, however many heroes are, and lost only when all four are. **A hero down does not stop a victory and costs its spoils nothing.**

`member.hp = maxi(hp, 20% of maximum)`: *the fallen refuse to stay down*. The line does not read `dead`: a hero at 1 health and a hero at 0 leave alike. His maximum, his Mana as it stood and the banked carries are written as anyone's.

Runs AFTER the return, and it reads `hp > 0`, so the hero who fell is healed with the rest: **he walks out at 35% of maximum, not 20%** (15% `SLOT_HEAL_PCT`, and every relic on `victory_heal_pct` adds to it: the Chalice of Dawn 10, Martyr's Knucklebone 15, the Cracked Hourglass 5). `docs/master.html` and the record say 20%, the floor alone.

The draft gate reads `hp > 0` and is never false: the return above has already run. A hero who fell drafts as anyone does; the elite's cache, the zone boss's pick and every class's talent point take no account of a fall.
The killing blow (who fell, to what, from whom, for how much) is booked to the run's tally and printed on the run summary; it is bounded, and the oldest is kept.
All four down: `Profile.note_wipe`, `Run.clear_save`, the summary; the run is over and nothing carries.
No member stands at 0 after a won fight, so every between-fights reader meets the living alone. The `hp > 0` test here is never false on the map.
`fallen_hero: true` needs a member at 0 health and finds none, so the Cairn of the Fallen cannot be drawn. Nothing reads `fallen_hero: false`.
`damage_pct` floors at 1, so no event can fell a hero; `revive_pct` is written for the dead and meets none.
Offers *the fallen*, finds nobody, and answers *No one to use the Revive Potion on*. Its other branch, 50% of maximum, has no caller that can reach it.
The health bar has a colour for `hp <= 0`, and nothing reaches it on the map.
No key of its own: a fallen hero is a member at `hp` 0 (v15). The state exists on disk only inside a fight in flight; a victory overwrites it and a wipe clears the file.

A fight quit and resumed opens with the same hero down: the spawn seats him at 1 so every stamp reads him as the opening did, then lays him down through `_die()`. His death fires nothing but its animation (FOUND AT GH), and `_fallen_at_spawn` takes any member at 0, so a fall that lasted would play it at every fight. The one way a fight opens with a hero down today.
A fight resumed with all four down is decided at once, down the wipe's path.

`fell` names each hero who fell (a hero raised still counts) and each hero row carries `fell` and `standing`. **The readout counts a fall and never its length, nor what raised him**; and it is built after the spawn, so a hero laid down in a resumed fight books `standing` false with `fell` false.
The plate greys, the chips go, and the turn bar leaves him out. The only screen that ever shows a fallen hero.
The hero sheet, the bargain's card (`offer_screen.gd`) and the map's target picker read `member.hp` as a number and have no fallen state: none can meet one.

The sim runs the same two doors, with no save and no Revive Potion (its bot drinks a Health Potion under 35%); `hero_deaths` books a death on the hero side, a companion's included, by tier, and the run report prints it.
